subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & pilot next steps (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & pilot next steps (FinBot)

Alex — thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap from my side to make sure we captured the right priorities and so we can align next steps.

Key pain points you shared:
- Unit economics: generation and embedding costs for user-facing features are eating margins (esp. high QPS on embeddings).
- Latency sensitivity: product needs p95 generation latency <200ms for the core flow (search/assist).
- Ops complexity: current homegrown autoscaling is unpredictable and expensive at peak.
- Procurement timeline: evaluating vendors now with a Q4 pilot target and potential procurement in early Q1.

Current stack you mentioned:
- Model hosting: self-hosted on AWS instances (mixed GPU types: g4/gn4), running an open LLM for generation and a hosted vector store for embeddings.
- Batching: some manual batch jobs but mostly single-request inference for low latency paths.
- Monitoring: Datadog + internal dashboards.

Success criteria for a pilot:
1) Reduce per-embedding unit cost by ~40-50% while maintaining embedding quality.
2) Keep p95 generation latency under 200ms in the interactive flow.
3) Demonstrate safe fallbacks & routing (e.g., lower-cost model variant during spikes) and easy rollout controls.
4) Minimal engineering lift to integrate (SDK + a short config).

Technical notes we captured from the call:
- You're open to quantized model variants (int8/4 where available) if quality holds.
- Prefix/KV caching is desirable to reduce repeated compute for common prompts.
- You're comfortable tolerating slightly higher latency for background batch jobs in exchange for cost savings.

Proposed next steps:
- I attached a short cost-model template (redwood_cost_model_template.xlsx). Please drop in your current usage numbers (QPS, avg tokens, embedding volume) and we’ll return an optimized config estimate.
- If it looks promising, schedule a 1-2 week pilot: we’ll provide a pre-configured Dedicated trial environment, sample quantized model variants, and a quick integration guide.
- Technical deep-dive with Dev (your engineering lead) to discuss batching, caching, and quantization trade-offs - can we target next-week availability?
- I’ve attached our SOC 2 summary for procurement.

Attachments: redwood_cost_model_template.xlsx, redwood_soc2_summary.pdf

Thanks again - happy to jump on a call with Dev and your infra lead to scope the pilot.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Rivera <alex@finbot.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & pilot next steps (FinBot)

Marissa - appreciate the recap, this is great and aligns with what we discussed. Quick replies inline:  

- I’ll fill out the cost template today and share numbers (current avg embedding QPS ~120, generation QPS ~45, avg tokens per generate ~180).
- We are definitely open to int8 quantization for embeddings and generation as a first pass; we’ll need to validate on our eval prompts.
- Dev (cc’d in my internal notes) is available for a technical deep-dive next Wed (8/25) morning PST.
- Procurement: we need vendor security docs for the board review - your SOC 2 summary helps, but procurement may request additional evidence (can you share your data retention and audit-log docs if available?).

Let’s aim to kick off the pilot in mid-September if the cost model looks good.

Thanks - Alex
